**Withhold approval for the registration/export changes. The direct-enum guard is sound in isolation, but completeness still has a gap.**

- **P2 — Cross-file constructors silently lose schema evidence.** [registration.go:97](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/terraform-provider-xcsh-2421-retrieval-enums/tools/pkg/docconstraints/registration.go:97) requires the receiver assertion in the factory’s file and records registration under that filename. [export-doc-constraints.go:53](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/terraform-provider-xcsh-2421-retrieval-enums/tools/export-doc-constraints.go:53) looks it up using the schema’s filename. Moving `NewThing` into `constructors.go` while keeping `Thing.Schema` and its assertion in `thing.go` therefore removes previously exported fields. Even duplicating the assertion leaves the filename mismatch. Bind registration by package/receiver identity, then associate schema destinations.

- **P2 — Indirect dynamic enums can still receive complete coverage; pre-existing gap.** In [enum.go:349](/data/robin-GIT/worktrees/terraform-provider-xcsh-2421-retrieval-enums/tools/pkg/docconstraints/enum.go:349), `[]validator.String{sv.Any(savedValidator)}` passes: `LiteralEnums` returns no evidence, the import is official, and the argument contains no call expression. If `savedValidator` holds `sv.OneOf(values...)`, coverage incorrectly becomes `true`. `sv.All(savedValidators...)` has the same problem. Unresolved combinator inputs must return incomplete coverage.

The inspected guards correctly reject shadowed factory identifiers, duplicate factory declarations, conditional constructor bodies, wrong role imports, unlisted receivers, and mismatched schema response/literal roles.

Remaining proof gaps: registration tests lack positive cases for datasource/action/ephemeral roles, provider-schema retention, and an end-to-end split-file destination case. Full method signatures and build selection remain unverified; this establishes declared source evidence only.
